root_cause.text: The osnoise tracing code acquired interface_lock before cpus_read_lock in configuration and hotplug paths, creating an inconsistent lock ordering with CPU hotplug’s cpus_write_lock → kthread_stop/wait_for_completion path, which can deadlock when the osnoise kthread also tries to take interface_lock.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly shows the deadlock chain: task1 holds mutex_lock(&interface_lock) then waits on cpus_read_lock, while CPU offline holds cpus_write_lock and waits for task3 to finish, and task3 in osnoise_sleep() tries to mutex_lock(&interface_lock); the patch fixes this by swapping the order of cpus_read_lock() and mutex_lock(&interface_lock) in trace_osnoise.c.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix lock ordering in osnoise_hotplug_workfn() by taking cpus_read_lock before interface_lock to avoid concurrency issues.
intent_record.what: The order of two scoped guard acquisitions in osnoise_hotplug_workfn() was changed so that guard(cpus_read_lock)() is now executed before guard(mutex)(&interface_lock), whereas previously the mutex guard was taken first.
intent_record.how: At runtime this changes the lock acquisition order to take the CPU hotplug read lock before the interface mutex, which can prevent lock ordering problems such as deadlocks or lockdep warnings when this function runs concurrently with other code that acquires these locks in the expected order.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder locking in osnoise_options_write() to take the CPU hotplug read lock before the interface mutex and prevent lock-ordering issues during option updates.
intent_record.what: The call to mutex_lock(&interface_lock) was moved to occur after cpus_read_lock() instead of before it within osnoise_options_write(), while the surrounding logic and comments remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime this changes the lock acquisition order so the CPU hotplug read lock is taken before the interface mutex, which helps synchronize option updates with CPU hotplug readers using a consistent locking sequence and avoids lock-ordering problems such as deadlock risks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the unlock order in osnoise_options_write() by releasing interface_lock before dropping the CPU read lock.
intent_record.what: The order of two unlock operations was changed so that mutex_unlock(&interface_lock) is called before cpus_read_unlock() instead of after it.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes lock release sequencing so the interface mutex is released while still holding the CPU read-side lock, then the CPU lock is dropped last, which can correct lock ordering and avoid synchronization problems such as invalid nesting, lockdep complaints, or races during option updates.

intent_record.intent_summary: Acquire the CPU hotplug read lock before the interface mutex when updating osnoise_cpumask to fix lock ordering and protect the update against concurrent hotplug access.
intent_record.what: The change moves mutex_lock(&interface_lock) to occur after cpus_read_lock(), and correspondingly moves cpus_read_unlock() to occur after mutex_unlock(&interface_lock), reversing the nesting order of the CPU read lock and the interface mutex around cpumask_copy(&osnoise_cpumask, osnoise_cpumask_new).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now acquires the CPU hotplug read-side lock before taking the interface mutex and releases the mutex before dropping the CPU read lock, ensuring the cpumask update happens while CPU hotplug protection is already active and aligning lock acquisition/release order to avoid unsafe lock ordering or races with CPU hotplug operations reading osnoise_cpumask.

grouping_result.intent: Acquire the CPU hotplug read lock before the interface mutex when updating osnoise_cpumask to fix lock ordering and protect the update against concurrent hotplug access.

consistency_review.core_intent: Ensure osnoise option and cpumask update paths use the correct CPU hotplug read lock and interface mutex ordering, including matching unlock order, to avoid lock-ordering and concurrent hotplug issues.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the reported deadlock root cause by reordering osnoise paths to take cpus_read_lock before interface_lock, and by matching the corresponding unlock order in option and cpumask update/hotplug code.

candidates.rationale: This acquires interface_lock before the CPU hotplug read lock in the hotplug work function, creating the lock-order inversion that can deadlock against CPU hotplug paths holding cpus_write_lock and waiting on osnoise threads.
This takes interface_lock before cpus_read_lock in osnoise_options_write(), directly embodying the inconsistent lock ordering described in the root cause.
This takes interface_lock before cpus_read_lock in the osnoise_cpumask update path, again establishing the problematic lock ordering with CPU hotplug.

The pre-fix unlock order mirrors the incorrect acquisition order; dropping the CPU hotplug read lock before releasing interface_lock is part of the same locking discipline error fixed to maintain consistent ordering.
In the vulnerable code this lock is taken only after interface_lock, making it the second half of the inversion in the cpumask update path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement acquires interface_lock before the CPU hotplug read lock in osnoise_options_write(), creating the inconsistent lock ordering at the core of the deadlock root cause.

This statement takes interface_lock before cpus_read_lock in osnoise_hotplug_workfn(), reproducing the same lock-order inversion against CPU hotplug paths that can hold cpus_write_lock and wait on osnoise threads.
This CPU hotplug read lock acquisition is vulnerable in context because it occurs only after interface_lock has already been taken, completing the inverted locking order in the cpumask update path.
This unlock reflects the pre-fix locking discipline by dropping the CPU read lock before releasing interface_lock, reinforcing the incorrect lock nesting that was fixed for consistency.
